messages:
incident-bot: Paging: runtime-prod-canary p95 token-generation latency breached 800ms (alert: RUNTIME_CANARY_P95_LATENCY). See metrics: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/alerts/runtime-canary

ravi (oncall): I got the page, looking now. pinging runtime eng.

alice (runtime): On it. We pushed batch-optimizer v2.3 to canary pool canary-01 at 02:17 UTC as part of the rollout. Initial hypothesis: batching change + kernel selection causing fallback thrash.

sara (support): FYI, Support has three customers reporting slow responses (timeouts / long tails). One is labeled P1 (customer: Skymap).

ravi (oncall): Reproducing quick checks: top-of-stack shows increased queueing on canary hosts, CPU OK, GPUs showing unusual kernel fallback logs. Pulling runtime logs now.

alice (runtime): Which hosts? I can grep the deploy logs and rollback if needed. Also we have a feature flag for continuous batching: `ff.continuous_batching` — we can flip it fast if needed.

ravi (oncall): Hosts: canary-01a/01b/01c. Logs: `kernel_fallback: selected_fallback_kernel=true` repeated in 1m, and `batch_size_adjust: -1 -> 0` entries.

alice (runtime): That's consistent with a kernel negotiation mismatch where the new batching path requests a quantized kernel variant that isn't available on the older CUDA driver, causing fallback to a slower path.

pm-connor: Any ETA on rollback/kill-switch? Customer visibility high, need short status for exec/CS.

ravi (oncall): Two short mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag `ff.continuous_batching=false` (fast, low-risk) 2) roll back batch-optimizer v2.3 deploy (takes longer, needs deploybot). Recommend flag flip first to rapidly reduce batching pressure.

alice (runtime): Agree. I'll prepare the flag toggle. Command to disable (internal API):

```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  https://flags.redwood.ai/api/flags/ff.continuous_batching/disable
```

ravi (oncall): Do it and we watch p95. If no improvement in 3 minutes, initiate rollback.

alice (runtime): Executing now.

[alice (runtime) posted a message with action emoji :rocket: at 02:46:12]

alice (runtime): `curl` returned 200. Flag disabled. Flipping internal config for canary.

incident-bot: runbook note: following mitigation step 1 (disable continuous batching).

ravi (oncall): Observing metrics... p95 dropping from ~920ms -> 410ms over one minute. Good sign.

sara (support): Skymap says response times improved on their end. They removed the escalated tag.

alice (runtime): Checking logs for kernel fallback entries: they drop sharply after flag flip. Looks like the continuous batched path triggered kernel selection that wasn't stable. With it off, we stay on the older, stable kernel.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment (batch-optimizer v2.3) remains tagged `deployed: canary-01`. No automatic rollback executed.

ravi (oncall): Given the quick improvement and customer reports, continuing to monitor. I'm going to patch the incident ticket and notify product.

pm-connor: Thanks. Quick ask: can we estimate blast radius and whether dedicated/dedicated-customers could have seen it?

alice (runtime): Blast radius limited to canary pool (only traffic routed to canary-01). Dedicated clusters were not part of this rollout. I'm running a quick scan of release config to confirm no config drift.

alice (runtime): Confirmed: only canary boolean was targeted. No dedicated or private deployments impacted.

ravi (oncall): Customer impact summary for now: 3 customers affected briefly, one P1 de-escalated after mitigation. We'll keep CS looped.

lee (oncall-next): Picking up handoff in 10m. Anything I should prioritize after monitoring window?

alice (runtime): Action items for next oncall: 1) schedule immediate rollback of batch-optimizer v2.3 from canary if we want to be conservative (deploy bot), 2) create a backport/compatibility test for kernel selection that exercises older drivers, 3) audit feature-flag rollout rules to ensure per-region gating.

ravi (oncall): I'm going to start the post-incident ticket with timeline. Will hand off to @lee in 10m for follow-up.

sara (support): CS has notified affected customers and provided workaround (retries and note about temporary latency). They want a follow-up postmortem.

alice (runtime): I'll prepare a minimal repro and some logs to attach. Looks like the root cause: the optimizer assumed presence of a quantized kernel that failed negotiation on this CUDA version, leading to fallback into slower code path under load, exacerbated by aggressive batching. Fix plan: add kernel capability check in negotiation, and tighten canary rollout gating for kernel/driver combos.

ravi (oncall): Monitoring still stable after 12 minutes. p95 ~ 380-420ms. No new pages in the last 6 minutes. I'll mark incident as mitigated but not resolved.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: MITIGATED (mitigation: feature flag disable). Link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-1839000123

lee (oncall-next): Took handoff. I'll own follow-ups: create rollback job if we decide, schedule postmortem meeting, and add tests.

pm-connor: Please include timeline + customer list in the postmortem. Also include decision rationale for flag vs. rollback.

alice (runtime): Will do. Tentative root-cause line for postmortem: "Batch-optimizer v2.3 introduced a batching path that attempted to select a quantized kernel without verifying driver/architecture compatibility, causing kernel fallback to a slower execution path which increased p95 under production canary load."

ravi (oncall): I'll attach monitoring graphs and the sequence of commands to the ticket.

sara (support): CS will wait for the postmortem before closing customer comms.

incident-bot: Next steps checklist added to incident: [ ] rollback decision, [ ] repro + tests, [ ] compatibility gating, [ ] customer PM follow-up.

ravi (oncall): Closing active page. Continue to monitor for 1 hour. If any regression, reopen.

[thread closed for now, handoff to lee (oncall-next)]
